Nicotinic receptor-mediated neuroprotection in neurodegenerative disease models. Multiple lines of evidence, from molecular and cellular to epidemiological, have implicated nicotinic transmission in the pathology of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review article presents evidence for nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR)-mediated protection and the signal transduction involved in this mechanism. The data is based mainly on our studies using rat-cultured primary neurons. Nicotine-induced protection was blocked by an alpha7 nAChR antagonist, a phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) inhibitor, and an Src inhibitor.
